source_text: ἔργα καὶ ἀπωλείας. Ἀπόβλητος οὖν, κἂν ἱερά τις εἴη ποτὲ καὶ ὁσία ψυχὴ, τοῖς οὕτως αἰσχροῖς ἐναλοῦσα μιάσμασιν. Ἀνίερον γὰρ κομιδῇ πᾶν ὃ ἐὰν γένηται μυσαρὸν καὶ μεμολυσμένον, διὰ τοῦ προσκεῖσθαι φαύλοις τε καὶ ἀνοσίοις ἀνδράσι. Γείτονα δὲ τούτῳ καὶ ἕτερον εὐθὺς κατεχρησμῴδησε νόμον· ἔχει δὲ οὕτως· «Καὶ θυγάτηρ ἱερέως, ἐὰν γένηται χήρα ἐκβεβλημένη, σπέρμα δὲ μὴ ᾖ αὐτῇ, ἐπαναστρέψει ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τὸν πατρικὸν αὐτῆς κατὰ τὴν νεότητα αὐτῆς· ἀπὸ τῶν ἄρτων τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτῆς φάγεται.» Ὁ μὲν οὖν τῆς ἱστορίας ἐναργὴς, οἶμαι, λόγος· ἰτέον δὲ δὴ πρὸς ἐννοίας τὰς ἔσω καὶ κεκρυμμένας. Εἰ γὰρ γένοιτο, φησὶν, ἀπόβλητος ὡς κατεγνωσμένη ψυχὴ, καὶ ἀνδρὸς ἐρήμη φαίνοιτο λοιπὸν, τοῦτ' ἔστι τοῦ νοητοῦ νυμφίου, καρπὸν ἔχουσα τὸν ἐξ ἀρετῆς οὐδένα· δρομαῖον ποιείσθω πρὸς τὸ ἐν ἀρχαῖς τὸ βάδισμα, καὶ ἐπανηκέτω γοργῶς ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἰδίου πατρὸς, διὰ μεταγνώσεως δὲ δηλονότι ζητοῦσα τὴν πρὸς Θεὸν οἰκείωσιν, καὶ τότε φάγεται τῶν ἄρτων αὐτοῦ. Λυπεῖ δὲ οὐδὲν καὶ οἷς ἔφαμεν ἀρτίως τὴν τῶν εἰρημένων ἐφαρμόσαι δύναμιν. Εἰ γὰρ γένοιτο, φησὶν, ἱεράν τε καὶ ἁγίαν ψυχὴν ἀνδράσι βεβήλοις ὑπενηνεγμένην κατολισθεῖν εἰς πλάνησιν, καὶ δογμάτων ἀλλοτρίων εἰσδέξασθαι μολυσμὸν, γένοιτό τε διὰ τοῦτο ὥσπερ τις χήρα καὶ ἀπόπεμπτος ἐκ Θεοῦ, ἐκνήψασα δέ πως οἷς κατώλισθεν μάθοι, ἐπανηκέτω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα. Δέχεται γὰρ τοὺς πεπλανημένους, εἰ φαίνοιντο καθαροὶ τῶν εἰσκεκριμένων αὐτοῖς ἀνοσίων σπερμάτων, εἰ μηδὲν ἐπιφέροιντο τῆς τῶν πλανησάντων βδελυρίας λείψανον· συναγελάζει δὲ οὕτω τοῖς ἁγίοις προσκυνηταῖς, παρατιθεὶς ἑαυτὸν ὡς ἄρτον ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, βρῶσιν αὐτοῖς τὴν ζωοποιόν. Οἶμαι δὲ ἔγωγε καὶ ἕτερόν τι παραδηλοῦν τὸν νομοθέτην ἡμῖν διὰ τουτωνὶ τῶν νόμων. Προαναφωνεῖ γὰρ ὥσπερ τῆς Ἰουδαίων Συναγωγῆς τὴν ἀπόστασιν, καὶ τὴν ἐπὶ τούτῳ δίκην, καὶ τὴν ἐσομένην ἐπ' αὐτῇ κατὰ καιροὺς χρηστότητα, πρὸς ὑποστροφὴν ἀναφέρουσαν ἐλέῳ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἀνακομίζουσαν εἰς τὸ ἐν ἀρχῇ. «Θυγάτηρ» γὰρ, φησὶν, «ἀνθρώπου ἱερέως, ἐὰν γένηται ἀνδρὶ ἀλλογενεῖ, τῶν ἀπαρχῶν τῶν ἁγίων οὐκ ἔδεται.» Ὅσον μὲν γὰρ ἧκεν εἰς διδασκαλίαν καὶ μάθησιν, πατὴρ ὥσπερ τις τῆς Ἰουδαίων Συναγωγῆς, ὁ θεσπέσιος γέγονε Μωσῆς. Ἦν οὖν ἄρα θυγάτηρ ἱερέως· ἱερουργὸς γὰρ καὶ ὁ Μωσῆς, ἅτε δὴ καὶ ἐξ αἵματος καὶ φυλῆς ὑπάρχων Λευΐ. Ἀλλὰ γέγονεν ἡ τούτου θυγάτηρ ἀνθρώπῳ ἀλλογενεῖ. Ὀλίγου γὰρ παντελῶς ἀξιοῦσα λόγου τὰ θεόθεν διωρισμένα, καὶ σπερμάτων τρόπον τινὰ τῶν ἄνωθεν ἀλογήσασα, μεμελέτηκε διδασκαλίας, ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ταῖς ἑτέρων καρποφορεῖ γνωμοδοσίαις· ταύτῃτοι Θεὸς ἐπῃτιᾶτο λέγων αὐτῇ διὰ φωνῆς Ἱερεμίου· «Ἆρον εἰς εὐθεῖαν τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου, καὶ ἴδε, ποῦ οὐχὶ ἐξεφύρθης· ἐπὶ ταῖς ὁδοῖς ἐκάθισας αὐτοῖς ὡσεὶ κορώνη ἐρημουμένη, καὶ ἐμίανας τὴν γῆν ἐν τῇ πορνείᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ταῖς κακίαις σου, καὶ ἔσχες ποιμένας πολλοὺς, εἰς πρόσκομμα σαυτῇ.» Ἀλλὰ ταυτὶ μὲν ἀρχαῖα τῆς Ἰουδαίων Συναγωγῆς τὰ ἐγκλήματα· ἀδελφὰ δὲ τούτοις καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [cont. from s.12: (bearing in error the) works (ἔργον) of error and of destruction (ἀπώλεια).] Rejectable (ἀπόβλητος) then, even if a soul (ψυχή) were once sacred (ἱερός) and holy (ὅσιος), having been caught in (ἐν-ἁλίσκομαι, aor. ptc. ἐναλοῦσα) such shameful pollutions (μίασμα). For wholly unholy (ἀνίερος) is all that becomes abominable (μυσαρός) and defiled (μολύνω) through lying close to (πρόσκειμαι) base (φαῦλος) and unholy (ἀνόσιος) men. Neighbouring (γείτων) this he at once proclaimed (καταχρησμῳδέω) another law; it runs: 'And a priest's daughter, if she becomes a widow cast out (χήρα ἐκβεβλημένη; no ἤ in Cyril), and she has no seed (σπέρμα), she will return to her paternal house according to her youth (νεότης); from the breads of her father she will eat' [Lev 22:13]. The account of the history (ἱστορία) is plain (ἐναργής); we must go to the inner and hidden thoughts (ἔννοια). For if, he says, a soul becomes rejectable as condemned (καταγινώσκω), and appears thereafter bereft (ἐρήμη) of a husband, that is the intelligible bridegroom (νοητὸς νυμφίος), having no fruit (καρπός) from virtue (ἀρετή): let her make her walking at a run (δρομαῖος βάδισμα) toward what was at the beginnings, and return swiftly (γοργῶς) to the house of her own father, seeking through change of mind (μετάγνωσις) the appropriation/belonging (οἰκείωσις) toward God, and then she will eat of his breads. Nothing hinders (λυπεῖ οὐδέν) applying (ἐφαρμόζω) the force (δύναμις) of what was said to those we just mentioned. For if a sacred and holy soul, carried off (ὑποφέρω, pf. ptc. ὑπενηνεγμένην) by profane (βέβηλος) men, slips down (κατολισθάνω) into error (πλάνησις) and receives the pollution (μολυσμός) of alien doctrines (δόγμα ἀλλότριος), and becomes thereby like a widow and dismissed (ἀπόπεμπτος) from God, but having sobered up (ἐκνήφω) somehow learns into what she slipped, let her return to the Father. For he receives the strayed (πλανάω) if they appear clean of the unholy seeds introduced (εἰσκρίνω) into them, if they carry no remnant (λείψανον) of the foulness (βδελυρία) of those who led them astray; and so he herds them together (συναγελάζω) with the holy worshipers (προσκυνητής), setting himself before them (παρατίθημι) as bread from heaven, the life-making (ζωοποιός) food (βρῶσις). I think the lawgiver (νομοθέτης) also indicates (παραδηλόω) something else by these laws. He proclaims beforehand (προαναφωνέω) as it were the apostasy (ἀπόστασις) of the Synagogue of the Jews, the penalty (δίκη) for it, and the kindness (χρηστότης) to come upon her in due seasons, bringing her back to return (ὑποστροφή) by God's mercy (ἔλεος) and restoring (ἀνακομίζω) her to what was in the beginning. 'A daughter of a priestly man, if she becomes [wife] to an alien man (ἀνὴρ ἀλλογενής), will not eat of the firstfruits (ἀπαρχή) of the holy things' [Lev 22:12]. As far as teaching (διδασκαλία) and learning (μάθησις), the divine (θεσπέσιος) Moses became as it were father of the Synagogue. So she was a priest's daughter; for Moses too was a sacred minister (ἱερουργός), being of the blood and tribe of Levi. But his daughter became [wife] to an alien man. Deeming (ἀξιόω) of altogether little account what was defined (διορίζω) from God, and in a way disregarding (ἀλογέω) the seeds from above, she has practised (μελετάω) teachings, commandments of men (ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων), and bears fruit (καρποφορέω) to the opinions (γνωμοδοσία) of others. Therefore God accused (ἐπαιτιάομαι) her through Jeremiah's voice: 'Lift your eyes to straight ahead and see where you were not mixed/defiled (ἐκφύρω); on the roads you sat for them like a deserted (ἐρημόω) crow (κορώνη), and you defiled (μιαίνω) the land in your fornication (πορνεία) and in your evils; and you had many shepherds (ποιμήν) for a stumbling (πρόσκομμα) to yourself' [Jer 3:2-3 LXX]. But these are ancient charges (ἔγκλημα) of the Synagogue; and sibling (ἀδελφός) to these also [cont. in s.14].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …works of error and of destruction. So a soul is to be cast off, even if it was once sacred and holy, when it has been caught in such shameful defilements. For whatever becomes loathsome and defiled through attaching itself to base and unholy men is altogether unholy. Right after this he laid down another law, close to the first; it runs as follows: ‘And if a priest’s daughter becomes a widow, cast out, and has no offspring, she shall return to her father’s house as in her youth; she shall eat of her father’s bread’ (Leviticus 22:13). The historical sense, I think, is plain; but we must go on to the inner and hidden meanings. For if, he says, a soul should be cast off as condemned, and is seen from then on to be without a husband, that is, without the spiritual Bridegroom, and bears no fruit of virtue, let her hurry her steps back to what she was at the beginning, and let her return quickly to her own father’s house, seeking, that is, through repentance, to belong to God; and then she will eat of his bread. Nothing prevents us from applying the force of these words also to those we spoke of a moment ago. For if, he says, a sacred and holy soul, carried away by profane men, should slip into error and take in the defilement of alien doctrines, and so become like a widow, sent away from God, but should then somehow come to her senses and learn what she has slipped into, let her return to the Father. For he receives those who have strayed, if they prove clean of the unholy seeds sown in them, and if they carry no trace of the foulness of those who led them astray; and so he gathers them into one flock with the holy worshipers, setting himself before them as bread from heaven, their life-giving food (John 6:32–33). And I think the lawgiver also hints at something else to us through these laws. For he foretells, as it were, the falling away of the Synagogue of the Jews, the punishment that follows it, and the kindness that will be shown to her in due time, which by the mercy of God brings her back and restores her to what she was at the beginning. For ‘a priest’s daughter,’ he says, ‘if she is married to a man of another race, shall not eat of the firstfruits of the holy things’ (Leviticus 22:12). For as far as teaching and instruction go, the inspired Moses became a kind of father to the Synagogue of the Jews. She was, then, a priest’s daughter; for Moses too was a minister of sacred rites, since he was of the blood and tribe of Levi. But this man’s daughter became the wife of a man of another race. For she held what God had laid down to be worth almost nothing, and, in a manner of speaking, disregarded the seeds from above; she has studied teachings that are the commandments of men (Matthew 15:9; Isaiah 29:13), and she bears fruit for the opinions of others. That is why God reproached her, saying to her through the voice of Jeremiah: ‘Lift up your eyes and look straight ahead, and see: where have you not defiled yourself? By the roadsides you sat waiting for them like a lonely crow, and you defiled the land with your prostitution and your wickedness; and you had many shepherds, to your own stumbling’ (Jeremiah 3:2–3). These, however, are the ancient charges against the Synagogue of the Jews; and akin to them are also…

choices.why: 'οἰκείωσιν πρὸς Θεόν' rendered 'to belong to God'.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Section opens mid-sentence: 'ἔργα καὶ ἀπωλείας' completes s.12's 'καρποφοροῦντες ἐν πλάνῃ τὰ πλάνης' (bearing in error the works of error and of destruction); the s.12 translator should end so that '…works, and of destruction' joins cleanly. Lev 22:13: Cyril's text reads 'χήρα ἐκβεβλημένη' (widow, cast out) without the LXX's 'ἤ' (widow or divorced); rendered as he has it. The Migne print capitalises 'Πατρὸς' inside the first Lev 22:13 quotation; the literal referent is the woman's father, so lowercase in the quotation. 'νοητοῦ νυμφίου' rendered 'spiritual Bridegroom' (Christ). 'οἰκείωσιν πρὸς Θεόν' rendered 'to belong to God'. In 'Δέχεται … παρατιθεὶς ἑαυτὸν ὡς ἄρτον' the subject slides from the Father to Christ as the bread; English keeps the unspecified 'he'. 'Bread from heaven … life-giving' cited to John 6:32–33 (6:33: the bread of God gives life to the world). 'θεσπέσιος' rendered 'inspired' (old English had 'all-divine'). Moses' Levitical descent (Exodus 2:1; 6:16–20) is stated as fact, not quoted; uncited. 'διδασκαλίας, ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων' is the wording of Isaiah 29:13 LXX as quoted in Matthew 15:9. Jeremiah 3:2–3 follows the LXX: 'ἐξεφύρθης' (literally 'mixed/fouled yourself'), 'deserted crow' (Hebrew: an Arab in the wilderness), and 'you had many shepherds' (Hebrew 3:3 differs: showers withheld). Section ends mid-sentence; s.14 continues with 'new' charges. Review: s.12's English ends 'bear as fruit the…' without 'of error' (Greek τὰ πλάνης ends s.12), so s.13 opens '…works of error and of destruction' to make the join read whole.

changes: opening join supplies 'of error' (s.12 English stopped at 'the…')
ἀπόβλητος rendered as 'is to be cast off' (verbal adjective) with natural order
'like a widow, sent away from God' keeps the two predicates apart; 'learn what she has slipped into' replaces Greek word order
restored second 'if' (εἰ μηδὲν) and the γάρ before the Moses clause
'bears fruit to the opinions' -> 'for the opinions'
scripture checked: Lev 22:13, 22:12 LXX; John 6:32-33; Isa 29:13 LXX / Matt 15:9; Jer 3:2-3 LXX — all correct
